language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi there, my name is Nadir and I am an underwater archaeologist. I’ve always been fascinated by the sea and the many hidden wonders it holds.
My team and I have been searching for signs of the lost city of Atlantis. Atlantis was once a beautiful island, until one day it mysteriously sank into the ocean and it was never seen again.
Someone said that the Atlantians used very advanced industrial equipment and even had vehicles that could fly in the air and dive through the water using magnetic forces.
Today, I am exploring a possible Atlantis site for evidence of these magnetic objects.
I thought I would begin by making a list of some of the objects that use magnets in our world today.
There are so many uses for magnets, so I’ve narrowed them down to 3 categories: domestic uses, industrial uses and medical uses.
Let’s get suited up and dive in to help Nadir create his list of magnetic objects.

Did you know that the telephones use permanent magnets and electromagnets to cause vibration that carries sound waves so we can hear each other over long distances? I've made a list of a few other items that we use in our everyday lives. Will you help me decide which ones use magnets and which do not?

I had to return to the surface to bring some samples back to camp. While I was there I grabbed my journal to help with the final category...medical uses for magnets. I’ve begun pasting pictures but I still need to add how the magnets are used for each object. Do you think you can help me with that?

helperSimple.text: Choose the right description that matches the medical object shown.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What is the use of this medical magnet?

answers.text: Doctors use this machine to spin patients in circles to test how quickly they feel dizzy.
An MRI machine uses a powerful magnetic field to help doctors check your internal organs.
This machine uses crystals and ultrasonic waves to take pictures of your bones.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What is the use of this medical magnet?

answers.text: Cow magnets attract metal in the cow's food, protecting its stomach and heart from injury.
Cow magnets prevent the cow from eating too much food.
Cow magnets help the cow make louder sounds to ward off predators.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What is the use of this medical magnet?

answers.text: Hearing aids use magnetic attraction. It only works if the person you are talking to wears one too.
Hearing aids use magnets to pull the eardrum closer to the outer ear.
Some hearing aids use electromagnetic fields to create sound through inner ear bone vibrations.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: What is the use of this medical magnet?

answers.text: A Ventricular Assist Device uses electromagnets to spin a magnetic rotor, mimicing the heart's pumping function.
This magnetic device holds the heart together after surgery until stitches fully heal.
The magnets in this heart assist device use magnetic forces to sustain heart function in heart attack patients.

outro.text: Wow. You know a lot about magnets. I didn’t realize there were so many uses for magnets in medicine.
